topic: How can hybrid analog/digital beamforming architectures optimize power efficiency while maintaining spatial multiplexing gains?
consensus_response: Hybrid analog/digital beamforming architectures can optimize power efficiency while maintaining spatial multiplexing gains by leveraging the concept of 'beam space multiplexing' (BSM). BSM shifts spatial multiplexing from antenna domain to beam domain, achieving high power efficiency and capacity. By optimizing the analog and digital processing, we can minimize used power and bandwidth while maintaining spatial multiplexing gains. This enables efficient beam searching, tracking, reporting, and recovery in the analog domain. The received signal vector at the receiver can be expressed as y = hvs + n, where v ∈ cntr is the optimal beamorming matrix with r beams. The capacity can be written as cbeam = log2(1 + snrm2 1), showing high power efficiency gains.
